narration: [chintu] <bookmark mark='chintu'/>Bigger numbers give bigger squares, so with bigger numbers the answer grows.
<bookmark mark='trials'/>Six squared is thirty six, and five times seven is thirty five. Ten squared is one hundred, and nine times eleven is ninety nine.
<bookmark mark='strike'/>Both sets give exactly one, so the result does not grow at all.
removed_beats.on_screen: the hint card leaves; Chintu's bubble shows bigger numbers, bigger answer; the two trials 36 − 35 = 1 and 100 − 99 = 1 appear side by side; the bubble is struck in the warning colour

narration: <bookmark mark='c1'/>To check, try any three numbers in a row of your own choice.
<bookmark mark='c2'/>Then expand again, and see that the outer pair always gives n squared minus one.
removed_beats.on_screen: the stage clears except the anchor and the boxed identity; two check lines: try any three numbers in a row; expand the right side to n² − 1

old_misconception.wrong_move: Chintu guesses that with bigger numbers the answer grows. Every trial gives 1, because the outer two always multiply to one less than the middle squared.
